exposure: general practitioner (GP) public hospital shared care
midwifery continuity of care (MWCOC) in the public system
private obstetric (PO) care in the private system
outcome: postnatal visits at home by a midwife
feeling the care provider showed commitment
feeling the care provider knew them
admission of a baby to SCN/NICU
baby being given formula when chosen to breastfeed
cohort: The study included 3725 postnatal women who provided information on birth outcomes after giving birth in Australia during the COVID-19 pandemic.
finding: The best perinatal outcomes for women who gave birth during the COVID-19 pandemic were achieved for those accessing midwifery models of care, particularly when cared for by privately practising midwives.
mod_finding: Midwifery continuity of care and privately practising midwifery care led to lower rates of induction, elective and emergency caesarean births, and augmentation with oxytocin, while private obstetric care led to higher elective caesarean sections and lower spontaneous labour and vaginal birth rates compared to standard care.
